briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to today's climate briefing, July 30, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Extreme Climate Disasters Strike Korea and the World
sections.content: News released today clearly indicates that the Republic of Korea and the entire world are facing unprecedented climate disasters. Domestically, experts warn that the current heatwave, described as a 'cruel summer,' is just the beginning [1, 4]. Busan recorded its highest heatwave in 122 years [11], and Seoul is also forecast to experience a record-breaking heatwave of up to 37 degrees Celsius next week [90]. Tragically, an elderly person in their 90s died from a heat-related illness while working in a field in Gimje, Jeollabuk-do [86]. Globally, significant losses are being reported, with small island nations suffering 76 trillion Korean Won in economic damage due to climate change over the past 25 years [3, 103, 109]. The advent of a 'compound disaster era,' where heatwaves follow heavy rainfall, underscores the urgent need to establish proactive climate disaster response systems [23].

sections.title: ⚠️ Widespread Impacts of Climate Change and International Warnings
sections.content: Beyond heatwaves and droughts, climate change is having widespread impacts across natural ecosystems and all human activities. In the upstream area of Unmun Dam in Cheongdo, Gyeongbuk, extreme drought conditions have revealed the site of a village submerged 41 years ago [87]. Agricultural reservoirs in the Jeonnam-Gwangju region are also recording significantly lower water levels than average, leading to the activation of drought response situation rooms [91]. Internationally, low water levels in the Rhine and Danube rivers are affecting military movement plans [111], while the risk of wildfires is increasing in national parks like Yosemite [99], and climate change is identified as a cause of worsening wildfires in Canada [106]. Furthermore, the impacts of climate change are materializing in the agricultural sector, such as difficulties in blackcurrant cultivation in Ribena [95] and early almond harvesting in Kashmir [114]. In Osan City, warnings have been issued regarding the increased activity of infectious disease vectors due to climate change [13, 26].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts and Adaptation Strategies Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various domestic and international efforts continue to realize a carbon-neutral society and adapt to climate change. The Seoul Metropolitan Area Meteorological Administration is operating the 'Climate Change Science Talk! Talk! Camp' to raise public awareness [2, 8]. Various local governments, including Jecheon City and Incheon Yeonsu-gu, are fostering carbon-neutral citizen instructors and operating life-cycle-specific eco-schools, thereby expanding region-specific education and practices [31, 33, 40, 45, 46, 51, 52]. Furthermore, inter-agency cooperation is active, exemplified by the launch of the government-wide 'One Health' consultative body by the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency [6] and a carbon-neutral business agreement between Chuncheon Police Station and the Korea Institute of Climate Change Research [5, 19]. In the agricultural sector, concrete efforts to adapt to climate change are underway, such as the establishment of 'smart orchards' in Seosan, Chungnam [10], and the promotion of a pilot project for semi-alpine summer cabbage in Jangsu-gun [12, 20].

sections.title: ⚡ Renewable Energy Expansion and the Core Driving Force of Energy Transition
sections.content: Energy transition has become a core driving force in responding to the climate crisis, with a particular emphasis on the expansion of renewable energy and the role of hydrogen energy. Incheon City has applied for a public-led offshore wind power generation permit for 680MW to achieve carbon neutrality and energy transition in the Seoul Metropolitan Area [42]. In the 'era of 100GW renewable energy,' hydrogen is increasingly emphasized as a 'strategic asset, not an option, but a necessity' [53, 56, 58, 60, 64, 75, 78]. Australia has seen its renewable energy share reach 42.1%, resulting in a 47% drop in wholesale electricity prices [57]. China also saw its share of coal-fired power generation fall below 50% for the first time in the first half of the year, with renewable energy surpassing 40% [79], indicating an accelerating global transition to renewable energy. Domestically, various attempts are being made to build efficient renewable energy systems, such as using AI to enhance renewable energy forecasting [55] and allowing companies to flexibly choose power contract durations [63].

sections.title: 📰 Key Discussions and Policy Challenges Related to Climate Change
sections.content: Climate change is sparking multi-layered discussions beyond simple environmental issues, encompassing economics, society, and international relations. China is leveraging climate response to strengthen its dominance in the eco-friendly energy supply chain [16], and the ASEAN Secretary-General held talks with China's Special Envoy for Climate Change [104], demonstrating simultaneous international cooperation and competition. The American Enterprise Institute (AEI) has released the 'U.S. Extreme Weather and Climate Change Dashboard' to enhance access to information on climate phenomena [101], and the Barcelona Institute for Global Health published the 'Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change 2026 European Cities Report' to highlight the link between climate change and health [102]. However, with local governments' carbon neutrality implementation evaluations embroiled in 'self-scoring' controversies and actual reduction achievements remaining at around 40% of targets [39], ensuring policy effectiveness and transparency remains a crucial challenge.

briefing.closing: Through the climate-related news gathered today, we have confirmed the severity of unprecedented climate disasters and the multifaceted efforts being made domestically and internationally to combat them. Responding to the climate crisis is no longer a task that can be postponed; it is a shared challenge for humanity, requiring continuous attention and action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
